oracle.description: test_gate_tiers.py decides correctness: 25 tests, red at the starting commit because gate_tiers.py does not exist. A permissive stub that validates nothing and always reports ready fails 14. The stub that matters -- one treating the first fully-green tier as sufficient -- passes every other test and fails 3.

purpose:
Write templates/dispatch/scripts/gate_tiers.py so a packet may stratify its registered gates without shrinking the set that must pass.

agentops#2046 asks for fast attempt falsifiers, focused candidate gates, and one full suite -- and, in the same breath, that stratification does not skip the final required repository gate. Reconcile them by keeping the split strictly about ORDER. A plan may stop early; that is the point, since a cheap falsifier saves the suite it would have wasted. But candidate_ready must still ask for every granted gate, so stopping early can only ever mean 'not a candidate yet' -- never 'candidate on less evidence'.

The seam is TIER_ORDER = ('fast','focused','full') plus four functions:
  stratify(packet) -> {tier: [command_id, ...]} for every tier, validated against the packet's allowed_command_ids, which is the grant. A packet declaring no gate_tiers is NOT an error: every granted id lands in 'full', which is what every packet frozen before this row already meant.
  plan(packet) -> [(tier, [ids]), ...] in TIER_ORDER, empty tiers omitted. This is the run order, cheapest first, full last.
  unmet_for_candidate(packet, results) -> the granted ids that have not yet run green, in run order. results is any iterable of {'command_id','exit_code'}, drained once.
  candidate_ready(packet, results) -> bool, true exactly when unmet is empty.

stratify raises ValueError when the declaration and the grant disagree: an unknown tier name, an id not granted by allowed_command_ids, an id in two tiers, a granted id in no tier, or an empty 'full' tier. That last one is the criterion enforced at freeze time rather than at gate time.

The likeliest wrong implementation treats the first fully-green tier as sufficient. It passes almost everything and fails the falsifier. No receipt wiring, no CLI, no file I/O.
required_outcomes: a packet declaring no gate_tiers puts every granted id in 'full' and raises nothing
stratify returns all three tier keys, empty lists included, and never mutates the packet
stratify refuses an unknown tier, an ungranted id, an id in two tiers, a granted id in no tier, and an empty 'full'
plan is TIER_ORDER with empty tiers omitted, and 'full' is always last
candidate_ready requires every granted gate green, whatever the tiers
a result for an id the packet was not granted is ignored
candidate_ready is true exactly when unmet_for_candidate is empty

acceptance_properties.requirement: stratification reorders work and never reduces what must pass
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a fast-tier green alone mints a candidate, or any granted gate is dropped from the requirement

acceptance_properties.requirement: a tier arranges the grant, it does not widen it
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a tier may name an id outside allowed_command_ids, or a granted id may appear in no tier

acceptance_properties.requirement: packets frozen before this row keep their meaning
acceptance_properties.fails_when: an undeclared packet raises, or stops requiring every granted gate

acceptance_properties.requirement: the two candidate predicates are one definition
acceptance_properties.fails_when: candidate_ready and an empty unmet_for_candidate disagree on any stream

non_goals: wiring the tiers into hybrid_dispatch.py -- it is protected at the manifest level and is a coordinator hand-pass
changing any existing packet's gate set
running commands, git, or any subprocess
